data.narrative:
Dexterity is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Samir Menon, Robert Sun, and four co-founders, currently valued at $1.65 billion post-money on $291 million raised to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private and one public company operating in robotics and manufacturing, including same-stage peers Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and adjacent-stage companies Agile Robots and Nimble Robotics (both $1.0B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B to next-stage step-ups, implies a valuation of $3.1B based on the $1.6B last post-money round. The peer-median method across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields $1.4B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. These methods reflect the current market positioning of robotics companies at this development stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.2B (low) to $3.6B (high), with a median of $2.3B. This range reflects tension between stage-typical progression multiples and current peer trading valuations. Key uncertainties include revenue traction relative to peer benchmarks, capital efficiency trajectories post-Series B, and sector-specific dynamics in manufacturing automation adoption rates.
